title: Dakh, Soured-Milk Butter
author: Amina Savoura (Afrik)
desc: Freshly drawn cow’s milk left three or four days in a whole calabash with the neck cut off; when it has soured, the gourd is shaken for two or three hours until the dakh separates, distinctly, from the soured milk.
longDesc: Dakh is the soured-milk and butter base that several lakh and thiakry recipes call for without explaining. Cow’s milk, freshly drawn, goes into a large calabash left whole with only the neck cut off to serve as a spout (mpkh in Serer, gamba in Wolof). It rests three or four days. When it has soured, the calabash is shaken very long — two or three hours — and the contents are poured into a container: the dakh is separated from the soured milk, and ‘very distinct’. It is collected in pots and kept until used. Editorial safety note, not from the source: the page starts from raw, unpasteurised milk fermented warm for days; raw milk can carry pathogens, and this entry does not recommend it.
ingredients: Cow’s milk, freshly drawn — quantity not printed
1 large calabash (mpkh in Serer, gamba in Wolof), left whole, with only the neck cut off for a spout
equipment: Calabash with the neck cut off
steps: Put the freshly drawn cow’s milk into a large calabash left whole, with only the end cut off to serve as a spout.
Leave it to rest three or four days.
When it has soured, shake the calabash for a very long time — two or three hours.
Pour the contents into a container: the dakh is separated from the soured milk, and very distinct.
Collect the dakh in pots and keep it until use.
chefTips: The observable endpoint is the separation: the dakh appears distinctly apart from the soured milk.
‘Quand il a aigri’ (when it has soured) names the state but not how to recognise it — no smell, taste or pH is printed.
The calabash is kept whole; only the neck is cut.
commonMistakes: Judging the souring by days alone.
Stopping the shaking before a distinct separation appears.
Using raw milk without understanding the food-safety risk.
storage: Kept in pots until use; no storage time is printed.
healthBenefits: A traditional fermented dairy product; the source gives no nutrition data.
Raw milk carries a food-safety risk.
culturalNote: Dakh is the unpasteurised butter-and-soured-milk base of Serer and Wolof dairy tradition, as the page presents it. The research found no published pH, titratable acidity or sensory description for Senegalese lait caillé in practice; one 2018 paper on northern Senegal states that producers’ end-of-fermentation criteria are not described.
sources: Title as printed: ‘Dakh’, subtitle ‘Beurre local du Sénégal’. Byline: Amina Savoura. Publication: Afrik (afrik.com). Date: ‘Publié le 10 février 2017 à 15h22’. Yield: none printed. The page has no ingredient list; the method names only ‘Le lait de vache sitôt tiré’. SINGLE-PASS.

FERMENTATION RULE — PARTIAL CUE, stated plainly: the time is ‘trois ou quatre jours’; the cue is ‘Quand il a aigri’, which names a state and not a sign; the churning is time only (‘deux ou trois heures’); the separation cue is observable (‘le dakh se trouve séparé du lait caillé, et très distinct’). Not upgraded to a sensory cue.
Times: rest 3 days (the shorter printed figure), cook = 2.5 hours of shaking (midpoint of 2–3 hours); prep is a scheduling estimate. The yield of 8 is a scheduling estimate.
The editorial safety note about raw milk is the compiler’s, not the source’s.
